post.caption: The ton of gold was two. In August 1896, gold was found on Rabbit Creek in the Yukon, and Skookum Jim and Dawson Charlie were in the party that found it. The creek was soon renamed Bonanza. The steamship Portland docked in Seattle on July 17, 1897, and more than 5,000 people met 68 men carrying gold. About 100,000 people set out for the Klondike, and only 30,000 to 40,000 reached it. Mounties made each traveler bring about a ton of food and gear. In summer 1898, about 30,000 people lived around Dawson City. Reports said a ton of gold, but it weighed about two tons.
